problem: Geometry-augmented VLN policies typically expose only the geometry foundation model's terminal feature to the policy, and either keep unbounded history or recency-based windows of geometric KV states. Intermediate GFM representations and instruction-relevant older observations are left unused.
motivation: Spatial reasoning is central to VLN, and GFMs like VGGT expose a hierarchy of intermediate features, but how to use them and which history to retain is unresolved. Unbounded memory grows with trajectory length, while recency treats age as a proxy for utility even though earlier frames may hold instruction landmarks or reliable geometry.
key_idea: Select geometry along two axes: couple VGGT depths 11/17/23 to successive Qwen3.5-4B decoder layers, and retain VGGT global-attention KV states under a bounded budget by instruction relevance, geometric confidence and transition novelty.
insight: Multi-depth coupling matters because of representation diversity rather than injection count: injecting the terminal G23 at all three sites (Deep×3) drops to 42.1 SR versus 55.7 for hierarchical, and is even below the geometry-free policy (46.5). Navigation-aware retention at 900K gets slightly higher SR/SPL than the 8+48 recency window (+0.4/+1.4) with 39.73% less GFM-KV memory; leave-one-signal-out ablations show each signal contributes (confidence removal costs 2.1 SR).
method: Hierarchical GFM-VLM fusion: VGGT features at depths 11/17/23 are injected after Qwen3.5-4B decoder layers 0/1/2 as residual updates at image-token positions.
Per-depth adapter: RMSNorm and 2x2 patch grouping (8192-D), then an MLP adapter to 2560-D, a token-wise sigmoid gate, and a learned scale s_m.
Instruction relevance: the instruction is split into subgoal segments; each token's score is its max cosine similarity to a segment embedding, after centering both visual tokens and segments.
Geometric confidence: VGGT depth and point-map confidences are pooled to the token grid, mapped via 1-1/c, and combined by min.
Transition novelty: a frame-level descriptor is compared with its nearest other frame descriptor to give a novelty score shared by all patches of that frame, recomputed each step.

Budgeted selection: the three signals are z-scored per layer and summed with equal weights, then TopK is applied independently per each of the 24 global-attention layers under a total budget (e.g. 900K) split across layers by GHOST-style offline per-layer allocation.
Training: Qwen3.5 and the fusion modules are fine-tuned jointly on R2R+RxR while VGGT stays frozen (~100 h on 8×H100).

setting.backbone: Qwen3.5-4B (fully fine-tuned) + VGGT (frozen) with fusion adapters
setting.training_data: R2R and RxR training sets only; no additional navigation-specific external data (0K)
setting.observation: single monocular RGB stream (no panorama, odometry or depth)
setting.action_space: low-level discrete actions in continuous environment (VLN-CE)
setting.simulator: Habitat (VLN-CE) plus a real Unitree G1 humanoid

numbers.extra: trained on R2R+RxR only, 0K external data; 900K aggregate KV token budget

results: On R2R-CE val-unseen AdaGeoVLN gets 55.7 SR / 51.4 SPL, beating JanusVLN* (52.8/49.2) with no external data and a single RGB stream. On RxR-CE it gets 54.1 SR / 61.8 nDTW versus JanusVLN* 51.4 / 59.1. Hierarchical fusion adds +9.2 SR over the geometry-free policy, and Nav. 900K cuts GFM-KV memory by 39.73% relative to Hybrid 8+48.
limitations: Retention coefficients are equal and untuned; the ablations do not establish optimal weighting.
Ablations are on R2R-CE only, and the gain over Hybrid 8+48 is small (+0.4 SR) with worse OS and NE than the temporal baselines.
Real-world evidence is qualitative (two indoor trials) and relies on a remote workstation for inference.
